content:
Goal: From the main menu, go to Member Inquiry. Make sure the search mode is Member Number, search for the member identified by the memberId parameter, and stay on the search results page. The results table has the columns Member No., Name and Shares. From the row for that member, extract the Member No. cell as memberId (a string), the Name cell as memberName (a string), and the Shares cell as shareCount (a number). Anchor the row on the memberId parameter — the Member No. cell holds exactly that value — rather than on its position in the table. Include a checkpoint asserting that the results row has a Member No. cell whose text is the memberId parameter, written with the ${memberId} template so it is parameterised. Note the distinction: memberId is a caller-supplied parameter, not a value discovered on the page, so pinning a checkpoint to it is exactly right — the rule against locating by a value you are about to read does not apply to parameters. This capability's whole job is finding the right member, so landing on the wrong one must fail rather than pass. Do not click Select: everything this capability returns is on the results page, and opening the record would add steps that can fail for no benefit. Mark memberName sensitive because it is personal data, and mark memberId and shareCount not sensitive — the member number is this system's lookup key and is already declared a non-sensitive input everywhere else, so redacting it as an output would be inconsistent with the contract it is read from.

These checkpoints assert data read from this page rather than the structure of the page, so they would fail for every other member, amount or date this capability is later invoked with:

- Checkpoint 1 ("URL reflects a member number search for the given memberId parameter") puts the value you extracted as `memberId` in its `expected`.
- Checkpoint 2 ("Results table has a Member No. cell whose text equals the memberId parameter") puts the value you extracted as `memberId` in its `locator[0].name`.

Rewrite each one to assert structure instead. For a value you must not hardcode:
  - assertion "exists" on the same locator — proves the field is present;
  - assertion "textMatches" with expected "^\\$[0-9,]+\\.[0-9]{2}$" — proves it holds a dollar amount, without saying which;
  - assertion "textContains" against the static row label rather than the value cell.

Values of the declared input parameters are fine to assert — the caller supplies those, so they are part of the request rather than part of the page. Then call finish again.

content.content:
These checkpoints assert data read from this page rather than the structure of the page, so they would fail for every other member, amount or date this capability is later invoked with:

- Checkpoint 2 ("Results table's data row Member No. cell (first cell after the header row) equals the memberId input parameter") puts the value you extracted as `memberId` in its `expected`.

Rewrite each one to assert structure instead. For a value you must not hardcode:
  - assertion "exists" on the same locator — proves the field is present;
  - assertion "textMatches" with expected "^\\$[0-9,]+\\.[0-9]{2}$" — proves it holds a dollar amount, without saying which;
  - assertion "textContains" against the static row label rather than the value cell.

Values of the declared input parameters are fine to assert — the caller supplies those, so they are part of the request rather than part of the page. Then call finish again.
